Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Partner Upper-Body Superset Session for 2 lifters
Resource limits: one bench and barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar, two ergs, about 25 minutes.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Partner Upper-Body Superset Session

Two lifters, one flat bench with a barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar and two rowing ergs. The whole session should take about 25 minutes. You work as a pair: while Partner A is on the first exercise of a superset, Partner B is on the second, and then you swap; nobody waits for equipment if you keep the order.

Warm-up
Both partners start together with 5 minutes of easy rowing on the ergs, followed by 3 minutes of arm circles and band pull-aparts.

Superset A: bench press and dumbbell row (2 rounds)
Partner A loads the bar and does a set of 8 bench presses, which takes about 40 seconds. Partner B starts on the dumbbell row at the same time, 8 per side, also about 40 seconds. Then swap: A goes to the rows once B has finished with the dumbbells, and B takes the bench as soon as A racks the bar. After both exercises, rest 90 seconds before the next round. Do 2 rounds, resting after each.

Superset B: overhead press and pull-ups (2 rounds)
Move straight on after the last rest. Partner A does 8 strict overhead presses with the dumbbells, about 45 seconds, while Partner B does a set of pull-ups, 6 to 10 reps, about 30 seconds. Swap when both are done: A moves to the pull-up bar, and B takes the dumbbells when A sets them down. Rest 2 minutes between rounds; there is no rest after the second round.

Cool-down
Finish together with 5 minutes of stretching: doorway chest stretch, lat stretch on the pull-up bar, and slow shoulder rolls.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

```

**Read-back**

This is one ~25-minute partner upper-body superset session for exactly **two lifters** working simultaneously as a pair, assembled from four blocks — a shared warm-up, Superset A, Superset B and a shared cool-down — and the source text reads as **complete**: the warm-up, both superset rounds with their swap rules and rests, and the cool-down are all present, so I'm not filling any gap. Both partners start together with 5 minutes of easy rowing on the **two ergs**, then 3 minutes of arm circles and band pull-aparts; Superset A is 2 rounds in which the **bench press** (~40 s, 8 reps) and the **dumbbell row** (~40 s, 8 per side) run *at the same time*, one partner on each, then they swap as soon as the bar is racked and the dumbbells are set down, with a **90-second rest after each round**; Superset B is 2 rounds in which **8 overhead presses** with the dumbbells (~45 s) run against **6–10 pull-ups** (~30 s), swapped only **when both are done** — so whoever finishes early holds (pull-ups take ~30 s vs ~45 s on the presses) — with a **2-minute rest between rounds and none after the second**, and then both finish together on 5 minutes of chest/lat/shoulder stretching. There is **no wall-clock finish time**: the deadline is "as early as the work allows," and the arithmetic (8:00 warm-up + ~5:40 Superset A + ~4:30 Superset B + 5:00 cool-down) puts the practical floor around 23 minutes against the ~25-minute target. The binding limits are the **singleton equipment** — one flat bench with barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar (plus two ergs for the shared warm-up) — held by **two athletes who must alternate on each station rather than queue**, and the explicit **hold points**: the 90 s post-round-A rest, the 2 min between B rounds, no rest after the final B round, and the "wait for both before swapping" barrier in Superset B.

**The model, restated**

A **track** is one sequential line of work — one station, one person, one instrument — and steps inside a track never overlap, so anything that genuinely happens *while* something else is happening (the two partners on two different stations, or a bench set running against a row set) has to live in its own separate track. A **step** carries exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with `seconds` (the 40 s bench set, the 5 min row), `variable` with `minSeconds`/`maxSeconds`/`defaultSeconds` (the 6–10 rep pull-up set, where I need a planning default), or `indefinite` (runs until the person ends it) — never two kinds at once. A **startTrigger** is what ties a step to the clock or to another step: `programStart` and `programStartOffset` for absolute time, `afterStep` / `afterStepWithBuffer` to chain off another step's end (optionally with an offset, or `event: "start"`), `manual` for a user tap, `onAbort` for the failure path, and `compound` to wait for all — or the first — of several triggers. **`stepId`s are unique across the whole program**, not per track, so two tracks can't both own a step called `press`; the parallel lines are named apart. Every `task` a step occupies needs a matching **`resourceConstraints`** entry, and that entry's `maxConcurrent` is the whole point here: it is what stops both lifters grabbing *the* barbell, *the* pair of dumbbells or *the* one pull-up bar at the same instant, and what makes the runner serialize them instead. Finally, work repeated n times is **`replicates: {count: n, mode: "serial" | "parallel" | "stagger"}` on one step** rather than n hand-copied steps — you chain each repetition onward with `{"instances":"each"}`, collapse the fan-in with `{"instances":"all"}`, and where the holding area between repetitions only fits k at a time you set `replicates.maxInFlight: k` so the upstream step is held back instead of stranding a downstream one; the same `"all"` barrier is also how the "swap only when both are done" rule in Superset B is expressed.

**Resource constraints I expect this workout to need**

Two people are working, so anything both partners use *simultaneously* gets `maxConcurrent: 2`, and anything that physically exists once gets `maxConcurrent: 1`.

- `erg` — **2** (two rowing ergs; both partners row the 5-minute warm-up side by side, and this is also the only genuinely parallel shared-equipment block)
- `mat` — **2** (floor space: the 3 minutes of arm circles/band pull-aparts and the 5 minutes of cool-down stretching are done by both partners at once; I'm folding the pull-apart bands into this area rather than inventing a separate shared band count the source never specifies)
- `bench` — **1** (one flat bench with one barbell — the singleton that forces A to rack the bar before B takes the bench)
- `dumbbells` — **1** (one pair, deliberately one task shared across Superset A's row *and* Superset B's press, since it's the same physical pair being handed over both times)
- `pullup-bar` — **1** (one bar; the singleton inside Superset B, and the 30 s pull-up set is the short side that holds for the 45 s presser)

    { "task": "erg", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "mat", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "bench", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "dumbbells", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "pullup-bar", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 2
}
```

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.
